In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the regulation of gene expression in the lung.
the molecular control of elastin gene expression.
the molecular mechanisms that control the transcription of elastin in the developing and adult lung and the role of elastin in pulmonary function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of elastin is regulated at multiple levels and that the regulation is complex and multifaceted.
elastin expression is controlled by a complex interplay between cell type, cell phenotype, age, and extracellular matrix.
the expression of elastin in the pulmonary airways is controlled by multiple factors and mechanisms, including cell-, age-, and phenotypic-dependent differences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of elastin is regulated by a complex network of transcription factors and co-factors, and that this network is highly dependent on cell-, age-, and phenotypic factors.
the transcriptional control of the elastin gene in the lung is highly complex and that the mechanisms that regulate elastin expression are likely to be cell-, age-, and/or phenotype-specific.

the control of elastin expression and deposition in the lung and vascular systems is a complex process that involves the coordinated expression of several elastin-related genes, the presence of specific transcriptional regulators, and the availability of appropriate extracellular microenvironments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are significant differences between the control of elastin expression in the lung compared to other tissues.

the expression of elastin and fibulin-5 is not simply regulated by the presence of TGF-β1, and that the expression of these genes is also regulated by the cell type and the phenotype that the cell has adopted.
there are significant cell- and age-dependent differences in the transcriptional control of the elastin gene in the lung.
